Though Pyle takes a frightening detour, Joker graduates to the Marine Corps and is sent to Vietnam as a journalist, covering, and eventually participating in, the Battle of Hue.

programme.title: A League of Their Own
programme.desc: Based on a true story, this film, set during World War II, tells the story of the all-female baseball league that was started while the American men were away fighting in Europe. After a team of potential players has been recruited, former player Jimmy Dugan coaches the girls and prepares them for the World Series.

programme.title: Wish You Were Here
programme.desc: When a perfect night with a perfect stranger ends suddenly the next morning, Charlotte searches for answers and meaning in her life. However, she soon uncovers a shocking secret that changes everything she knows about the man who captured her heart.

programme.title: The Cinema List: Animal Antics
programme.desc: Music and lights bring magic to life. From `Sing' to `The Bad Guys 2', enjoy animated animal adventures the whole family will love.

programme.title: Poison
programme.desc: A love story about a couple reunited years after tragedy drove them apart. Their brief and intense meeting brings simmering pain and resentment to the surface but is a reminder too of cherished intimacies and the love they once shared.

programme.title: Turn Me On
programme.desc: When a couple begin to skip doses of an emotion-suppressing pill, they rediscover life in all its unfiltered glory. However, this also forces them to deal with the baggage that comes along.

programme.title: Flashdance
programme.desc: A young female welder dreams of becoming a professional dancer and struggles against all the odds to realise her dream. However, in her effort to succeed, she discovers that getting to the top is far from easy. Giorgio Moroder's composition 'Flashdance (What a Feeling)', sung by Irene Cara, won an Academy Award for Best Original Song.

programme.title: All Is True
programme.desc: The year is 1613, and Shakespeare is acknowledged as the greatest writer of the age. But disaster strikes when his renowned Globe Theatre burns to the ground. Devastated, Shakespeare returns to Stratford, where he must face a troubled past and a neglected family. Haunted by the death of his only son, Hamnet, he struggles to mend the broken relationship with his wife and daughters. In so doing, he is ruthlessly forced to examine his own failings as a husband and father.

programme.title: Quartet
programme.desc: An opera star arrives at a performers' retirement home amidst fraught preparations for a fundraising concert. Her presence adds to the tension, but it also offers an opportunity to reunite a successful quartet.

The pair must live in shelters and endure many hardships, but Chris refuses to give in to despair as he struggles to create a better life for himself and his son.

programme.title: 16 December
programme.desc: 16 December 1971 was the day when India won the war against Pakistan and was able to liberate Bangladesh from Pakistan's rule. When the ruling dictator of Pakistan surrendered to India, some of the hard-lined Pakistani soldiers were bitter and angry at the surrender, as they wanted to continue fighting the Indians until their last breath. They retreated in silence and later came together to form their own groups of Jihadi soldiers to carry out terrorist attacks against neighbouring India.

Dessert is a true Anglo Italian affair with a ruby red plum and amaretti crumble. There is also an easy no-stir risotto with Nigella's farro risotto with mushrooms.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Five teams battle wind, waves, and time to sculpt monstrous sand creations. Six hours, one tide - who will survive this beach of horrors before they're all washed away?

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: A teenage boy rushes to help save a paralysed surfer from drowning; when a 999 call comes in, the Appledore crew are tasked with an immediate launch. In Little and Broad Haven, south Wales, there's a frantic search for two paddleboarders swept over a mile out to sea. The Hayling Island crew race against time to rescue a fisherman trapped in mud; two walkers in Redcar are cut off on a rapidly diminishing strip of beach; and in Porthcawl, a dog owner calls 999 after her dog is taken by the tide.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: A catastrophic dual carriageway collision brings two patients to Southmead Emergency Department: Tom, the driver who caused the crash, and Olli, the man whose van he hit. Tom, who is believed to have been driving under the influence of drugs and on the wrong side of the carriageway, arrives with devastating injuries to his leg. Meanwhile, a young girl is brought to Resus after falling from her horse, unable to move or feel her legs.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Ash reunites with Colin, and Gordon invites her - along with her eager boyfriend, David - to his birthday party at Echo Park Brewery, which is being thrown by his new girlfriend, Chelsea.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: BBC Weather
programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: Gosford Park
programme.desc: The late Robert Altman's Oscar-winning film is ostensibly a murder mystery set in a 1930s English country house, but the director also uses the plot to explore English sensibilities of the time. A stellar cast all shine without overpowering this very English film from one of America's best directors.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: The five celebrities face two more culinary challenges as they battle for a place in the quarter-final. First up, it's the return of the mystery box. Then, for the first time in their heat, they will have to cook to stay in the competition.

programme.title: BBC Wales Investigates
programme.desc: More people are turning to social media for cheap sperm as fertility costs soar. But a BBC investigation reveals the pitfalls and dangers that some women face. Gemma Dunstan investigates the unregulated world of sperm donation.

programme.title: The Big Deal
programme.desc: The four remaining pairs face their biggest challenge yet in a deal that straddles Berlin and London, two of the world's leading art destinations. Who can make it through to the semi-final?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Bienvenue to a very special episode of the show from Amiens in northern France! Twice a year, a huge fair bursting with antiquités takes over the city's streets, drawing 80,000 bargain hunters from across Europe. Among them are a red and a blue team of bargain hunters - one French and one British - ready for an international battle, the likes of which have not been seen since the Battle of Hastings!

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Blast off! Retro chairs meet galactic glamour as Sarah Peterson shoots for the stars with a cosmic revamp, but will this project soar or crash-land? Carpenter Kris sees potential in a pile of weathered fencing, and for his own project, JJ Chalmers attempts a tricky restoration job on a mid-century chest of drawers. Will all three upcycling projects produce profits?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his Belgian journey, Michael Portillo travels to Namur, capital of Wallonia, to discover a citadel dating back to the 10th century.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins his Hungarian adventure in the town of Sopron.

programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Angela Barnes, Kemah Bob, Ade Edmondson and Beattie Edmondson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman.

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: The game show that mixes general knowledge quizzing and bowling.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek and the team travel to the Elan Valley in Powys for a stunning seven-mile circular walk, punctuated by dams. He learns how the valley was flooded to supply water to Birmingham. On his way round he has a go at mountain biking and discovers the part the area played in the daring Dambusters attack in WW2. Meanwhile, archaeologist Dr Erin Lloyd Jones visits the ruins of the ancient abbey at Strata Florida.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: There's another milestone for Hazel, the first southern koala born in Europe. She has to be separated from her mother for a short period. This is to ensure that the keepers earn the baby's trust before she becomes impossible to work with. Without this, the park wouldn't be able to perform their routine and important health checks.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: 'Death in Paradise' star Ralf Little leaves the sun-drenched Caribbean well behind as he heads to the Orkney Islands off the north coast of Scotland to investigate his grandfather Arthur's experiences during the Second World War. Ralf is astonished to discover that Arthur was caught up in one of the most important battles of the war. Looking into another branch of his family, Ralf is thrilled to confirm a family rumour that he has a Welsh international footballer on his family tree.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The team of experts visit the spa town of Scarborough and discover a rare roll of Beatles wallpaper, the passport once belonging to the world's smallest man and examples of carved whales' teeth.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are at Wolverhampton Art Gallery. Experts Caroline Hawley and David Harper are on hand to value items and take them off to auction. Turning up out of the hundreds of bags and boxes is a jumble sale find that proves to be a valuable piece of jewellery.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Celebrity contestants James Buckley, Amy Gledhill, Romilly Weeks and Gary Wilmot take on a series of quiz rounds selected by Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round, and the scores are tallied across the week.

programme.title: Clive Myrie's Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive visits the bustling district of Vedado, the most modern and affluent part of Havana. He takes a motorcycle tour with Ernesto Guevara, Che Guevara's son, and finds out how to create an amazing feast even though Cubans live under rationing.

programme.title: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 1 highlights from the third Test match between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston.

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: Paddy McGuinness enjoys a lot of taste tests when he visits a factory in London to learn how they produce sticky toffee flapjacks on an epic scale.

programme.title: Britain's Forgotten Girls
programme.desc: Exposing the organised grooming and sexual exploitation of vulnerable British teenage girls, highlighting failures by the authorities for over two decades. Through survivor testimonies, it details how police and social services repeatedly failed to protect them.

programme.title: Mortimer and Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: While in Norfolk fishing for tench, Bob tries to impress Paul with his childhood fishing rod, and fails. They share nostalgia for their younger years and reveal how they recently came face to face with their own mortality. After a brief respite in a local brewery, they reluctantly camp down in yurts before fishing again the next day when the elusive tench seems to evade them until the very last minute.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Featuring extensive coverage of the day's top national and international news stories, along with explanations about the context and potential aftereffects.

programme.title: BBC Weather
programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: Couples Therapy
programme.desc: Orna sees Shay and Clinton separately to help them move forward. Sienna acknowledges her resentment for what Chris brought into their relationship. Marjorie and Jason work on listening to each other, and Drea has come to a decision.

programme.title: Couples Therapy
programme.desc: Sienna and Chris move forward with forgiveness. Orna coaches Marjorie and Jason through a fallout that stirs up Jason's painful past. Shay and Clinton make peace. Nessa and Drea try something new together.

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: During WWII, a resident is injured in a German minefield, while Edinburgh's post-war slum clearances threaten the house with demolition. Decades later, David reveals the building's extraordinary history to its current owners.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: It's the last quarter-final of the series, and this heat's remaining four celebrities return to do battle once more. They all want a place in the semi-finals, but only the best three will get there.

programme.title: Boom Town: How Merthyr Made the World
programme.desc: How did a small Welsh town become the heart of the Industrial Revolution? Steffan Powell explores five key factors, using new technology, CGI and AI to reveal Merthyr's hidden past.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Sue Kent head to Cambridge to help Susan and her sister Anita transform Susan's tired, deer-ravaged garden into a beautiful, deer-friendly wildlife haven. With rotten steps, a small patio and a lawn dominated by a bird bath and a dead apple tree, this once-charming space has become overrun by hungry deer. Susan has lived in her beloved home for 18 years, sharing it with local wildlife as well as the deer, who see her plants as a free buffet.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Upcycling expert Sarah Moore is at Beaconsfield Recycling Centre in Buckinghamshire, scouring the site for items that can be given a new lease of life rather than hitting the skips. Screen printer Zoe tries to turn soggy gazebo covers into plush cushions, while Larissa rolls up her sleeves to take a well-loved sofa from comfy to cool. For her own project, Sarah splits a sideboard in two to try to double its potential.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates a rewarding summer fruit harvest, proving that careful cultivation can triumph even in severe drought conditions. Carol Klein delves into the secret world of leaves.

programme.desc: On a mission to dig out some of his greatest adventures from the past, Derek revisits three memorable walks from mid-Wales. On his first wander, he is joined by opera singer Beverley Humphreys.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The park's Amur tiger breeding programme has been a huge success, with a male and female born three years ago. The precious cubs are now almost fully grown and nearing the age when they could be separated to start their own families. The latest addition to the park is one of the world's slowest mammals, a two-toed sloth. They have to build an enclosure to meet her exacting needs.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Andrew Lloyd Webber is a global superstar of musical theatre, still writing and producing blockbuster shows. He has also combined his nose for business with his love of architecture by renovating the Theatre Royal Drury Lane to its original condition. Andrew knows he comes from a musical family, including virtuoso cellist brother, Julian - but he'd love to find out where his showbiz genes and his love of musical theatre come from.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow team are in St Ives, a historic market town in Cambridgeshire, where finds include an early pocket calculator, a googly-eyed doll, a Clarice Cliff coffee set, some Crimean medals, and a pilot's logbook.
